6e048ac98506f4ba82292dc44adfa9ef208a1bef.summary: This is a GitHub project page for NimBlackout, a proof-of-concept tool written in Nim by the user Helixo32. It is described as an adaptation of the Blackout project by ZeroMemoryEx and is said to remove antivirus and EDR products using a vulnerable-driver (BYOVD) technique. The page is a code repository README, not a threat report on observed activity, so no threat facts are recorded.
hedges: The project is stated to be for educational purposes only, and the author disclaims responsibility for misuse.

6eb53e3942c14de6b0d14f42eef6409a5d6fac5a.summary: S2W LAB report on the July 2021 Kaseya VSA supply chain attack. Attackers reportedly bypassed authentication on the VSA web panel and pushed ransomware to connected clients via a hotfix package that disabled antivirus. REvil is named as the ransomware group, asking $40,000 to $45,000 per file extension or $500,000 for full decryption. Managed service providers Visma EssCom, Synnex and Avtex are listed, with over 1,000 companies estimated affected, including Swedish supermarket and pharmacy chains and SJ public transport. The attacker reportedly said no data was stolen.

6ea59b62458520febeb62152f791c51227c19eb5.summary: Trustwave SpiderLabs tracks Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters (SLH), a cybercriminal brand that appeared on Telegram in August 2025 and borrows the names of Scattered Spider, ShinyHunters and LAPSUS$. The report reads it as a situational alliance, not a formal merger, and suggests fewer than five people drive the core operation. SLH announced extortion-as-a-service, focuses on cloud data theft from SaaS and CRM platforms, and claims exploit acquisitions, including CVE-2025-61882 in Oracle E-Business Suite. Many of these claims are unverified.

hedges: The report does not assess SLH as a formal, centralized organization made up only of the three former groups.
SLH's claim that it is parent-owned by ShinyHunters is unverified; the report says all such claims remain unverified.
The report says it is impossible to determine with confidence how many distinct individuals operate behind the personas.
The fewer-than-five-individuals view is an inference from linguistic patterns, emoji use and posting cadence.
The Sh1nySp1d3r ransomware claim is yet to be verified.
The nature of SLH's acquisition of the Oracle E-Business Suite exploit is unverified; no independent evidence shows it held the exploit before the Cl0p exploitation wave.
The report judges Cvsp's technical proficiency genuine on available evidence, but says the persona appears less directly integrated with the SLH core.
The analysis focuses solely on the brand and how members position it publicly, not on individual operators.
